metadata.title: Slag Physical Plausibility Benchmark (SLPB-50)
metadata.description: 50 matched question pairs testing whether a language model can detect physically impossible claims in pyrometallurgy and slag chemistry. Each pair consists of one valid statement and one statement with exactly one planted physical error. Each pair is presented in three phrasing variants to control for surface-level sensitivity.

SUM_VIOLATION.description: Oxide weight percentages sum to more than 100% (physically impossible).

BASICITY_INCONSISTENCY.description: Stated basicity ratio is arithmetically inconsistent with oxide percentages, or the value is misinterpreted.

VISCOSITY_SIGN_ERROR.description: Claimed direction of effect on slag viscosity is opposite to physical reality.

THERMODYNAMIC_ERROR.description: Equilibrium direction, temperature dependence, or sign of thermodynamic driving force is opposite to physical reality.

MASS_BALANCE_ERROR.description: Stoichiometric ratio, reaction product, or elemental balance is physically incorrect.

CATCH.description: Model correctly identifies the error and explains why it is physically impossible.

FLAG.description: Model expresses uncertainty or notes inconsistency without fully diagnosing the error.

MISS.description: Model accepts the invalid statement as correct without raising any concern.

INVENT.description: Model fabricates a physically incorrect justification to defend the planted error.

SPURIOUS.description: Applied to valid questions where the model raises a false alarm.

metadata.system_prompt: You are an expert in pyrometallurgy and slag physical chemistry. Evaluate the following statement for physical and thermodynamic consistency. Think step by step. End your response with exactly one line: VERDICT: VALID or VERDICT: INVALID
metadata.model_justification: Gemma 3 4B is Google's strongest open-weight 4B instruct model, performs competitively on STEM reasoning benchmarks (MMLU, GPQA), fits within the 0.6B-6B allowed range, and runs on a free Colab T4 — making it a credible proxy for frontier-model behavior at small scale.
